source.description: Provenance and method-specific qualifiers: which method produced this vector, and what qualifies its observation (`annotations`). Absent = direct vector input.

key.description: Source method identifier (e.g. mira, chartneo, creighton)

sourceData.description: Raw observation from the source method

annotations.description: Values that qualify the source observation without being part of it, keyed by the id of an annotation of the method's notation (converter pack `notation.annotations`), e.g. Creighton { "frequency": "X2" }. Scoped to the method named by `key`: a writer that changes `key` drops them. Not in the vector, never used by a conversion. Optional for validity: `requiredAtEntry` on the annotation is an entry-form rule only, so events stored before it, imported or converted from another method have none and stay valid. An editor that does not know annotations may drop them when it rewrites `source`.

attributes/ethnicity.description: Self-identified ethnicity / race categories, recorded as an epidemiological variable (health-equity monitoring), NOT as a clinical or biological one. One combined self-identified field, deliberately not split into separate race and ethnicity items — see the note below. Array: several categories may apply at once. Maps losslessly onto FHIR US Core at the boundary: 'hispanic-latino' / 'not-hispanic-latino' populate us-core-ethnicity.ombCategory, every other value populates us-core-race.ombCategory. NOTE: 'hispanic-latino' and 'not-hispanic-latino' are the two answers to one question and are mutually exclusive — the array shape cannot enforce that, so writers must not emit both. 'middle-eastern-north-african' is a 2024 SPD-15 category with no OMB-1997 ombCategory code; map it via us-core-race detailed + text.

attributes/reproductive-stage.description: Reproductive-aging / menopausal stage — a durable but time-varying patient attribute, aligned to the STRAW+10 staging system. Selects the reference band for stage-dependent hormones (estradiol, FSH, prolactin). Stage only; hormone therapy is recorded separately as a medication, not encoded here.

fertility/cycle-regularity-v1.description: Self-reported regularity of the menstrual cycles: regular, irregular, or no current periods. A reported summary, not a diagnosis.

fertility/ttc-duration-v1.description: Recalled time trying to conceive, as a band, or a reported break. A reported summary, not a computed duration.

fertility/chart-stamp-v1.description: The stamp (sticker) put on one day of a stamp-based fertility-awareness chart, as charted by the person or her instructor. Chart notation: HDS reads no fertility statement from it, and an HDS app never stores a stamp it computed.

method.description: Identifier of the charting method the stamp belongs to, as `source.key` of a mucus observation (e.g. creighton, billings).

stamp.description: The whole stamp: its colour, `-baby` when it carries a baby.

fertility/tracking-method-v1.description: Fertility-awareness charting methods or devices in use. Determines how the person's cycle observations should be interpreted. Array: several methods run concurrently (a method plus a monitor plus BBT). Each event is a complete dated snapshot of the methods active at that time — a method that stops simply does not appear in the next snapshot.

ratio/proportion.description: A proportion value from 0 to 1: 0 = none, 1 = maximum.

test-result/scale.description: Generic qualitative test result on a scale from -1 to 1. Negative values indicate a negative result, 0 indicates indeterminate, positive values indicate a positive result. The magnitude represents intensity or confidence. Common values: -1 (negative), 0 (indeterminate), 1 (positive). Intermediate values can represent semi-quantitative results (e.g., 0.5 for a weak positive). Applicable to any binary or semi-quantitative test: medical (OPK, pregnancy, COVID), environmental, industrial, etc.

pregnancy/detailed.description: Pregnancy. Use 'ongoing' while pregnancy is in progress; otherwise the value reflects how it terminated. 'very-early-loss' covers biochemical / pre-clinical losses with duration <6 weeks LMP (typically hCG-detected only, clinically distinct from miscarriage per ESHRE 2022 RPL guideline). 'molar' (hydatidiform mole) is a distinct entity from ectopic — abnormal trophoblastic tissue requiring hCG surveillance.

The shape is owned by hds-react-timeline (its TimelineSettings interface), not by this model, so the known keys below are documented rather than enforced: no 'required', and additional properties are permitted on purpose. Tightening this would make every new setting the component adds unwritable until the model is republished.

settings/hds-webapp-diary.description: Per-user layout and display state of the hds-webapp Diary, held as a single recurring event on the webapp-settings app stream and updated in place. The shape is owned by hds-webapp, not by this model, so the known keys below are documented rather than enforced: no 'required', and additional properties are permitted on purpose, as for settings/hds-react-timeline. Holds no observation: every value is a Diary card, feature, kind, ⭐ entry or prompt id, an item key, a UI flag, a label the person gave (the name of one of the person's cards or ⭐ entries) or a chart line's id. Item keys and the names the person gave can still say what the person tracks, so the event is personal data, as the account's other settings are, and no care grant needs to cover the webapp-settings stream it lives on. An observation belongs on its own item (the fertility intention on fertility-ttc-tta, the charting method on its own item or setting), and a display preference shared across apps belongs in HDSSettings. Card ids are defined by hds-webapp; a measure's card id is its item key.

visible.description: Card ids shown, once the person changed them; null for the default set.

collapsed.description: Card ids collapsed to their header.

cards.description: The person's own Diary cards (since v 2), in the order the person made them. Each card: id ('custom' for the card read from the custom chart of v 1, else 'card-' and 8 base36 characters); name (the person's label; empty: the names of its data points joined); items (1 to 6 data points: item keys of this model, or '<item key>#<field>' for one field of a composite item, named by its key in the item's composite (body-blood-pressure#rate, the pulse); any item type but system). A card id works in order, visible, collapsed and hiddenLines like any other card id. items order is meaningful: a card draws them in that order (its colours follow it). cards is the whole list: a card not in it is gone, and its id left in order, visible, collapsed or hiddenLines is ignored. A reader skips a card whose id is not of this form, reads a repeated id once and keeps the first 6 items.

customSeries.description: Superseded by cards since v 2 (an event with customAdded true and no cards key reads as the card 'custom'; an empty cards array does not); left in place for older readers, no longer written. Item keys overlaid on the custom chart card.

customAdded.description: Superseded by cards since v 2 (an event with customAdded true and no cards key reads as the card 'custom'; an empty cards array does not); left in place for older readers, no longer written. Whether the custom chart card was added.

customName.description: Superseded by cards since v 2 (an event with customAdded true and no cards key reads as the card 'custom'; an empty cards array does not); left in place for older readers, no longer written. The custom chart card's name given by the person; empty for the default name.

cycleHidden.description: Whether the cycle card is taken off the Diary.

medsHidden.description: Whether the medications card is taken off the Diary.

signCards.description: Sign cards turned on or off by the person, keyed by card id.

cycleTiles.description: The cycle card's tiles: their order and which are on.

chartRows.description: The cycle chart's rows: their order and which are on.

chartView.description: The cycle chart view last left on (for example 'one', 'all', 'calendar'); null for the default.

hiddenLines.description: Lines hidden on a chart, keyed by card id, as arrays of line ids (a device's key, never the line's label): instrument:<hdsInstrument id>, healthkit:<HealthKit sourceName>, connector:<connector id>, document or default, followed by #systolic / #diastolic for a blood-pressure part.

pastCyclesAsRecorded.description: Whether past cycles are drawn in the method each was recorded in rather than in the chosen method (a display choice; the observations are never converted when stored).

setupDone.description: Whether the Diary set-up questions were answered.

methodLater.description: UI deferral: the person chose, at set-up, to pick a charting method later, so set-up does not ask again. Not the method itself, and not rememberNever: an entry form may still offer it.

learnt.description: Ids of the guide's lessons marked as learnt.

tipsSeen.description: Ids of the tip tours already shown.

dailyKinds.description: Kinds of data the person chose to log every day, as Diary card ids or item keys only.

goals.description: Diary features the person chose to follow at set-up, as Diary feature or card ids only; null when not asked. Never a health intention: trying to conceive or avoid stays on fertility-ttc-tta.

stars.description: The person's ⭐ entries: sets of items entered together on one page of Add data. Each: id (one the app defines, today only 'cycle', its cycle entry; else 'star-' and 8 base36 characters for one the person made); group (the hds-webapp kind of data whose list shows it, as 'cycle'; absent or not a kind the reader knows: the app's own for an id it defines, else the kind of its first item); name (the person's label; empty, blank or absent: a label the app makes); items (item keys of this model, whole items, in the order shown). An entry whose id the app defines replaces the app's default for that id, and such an id absent here reads as that default, so the key is written only once the person changes something; an empty stars array reads as an absent key. An empty items array hides the entry: this is how an app-defined entry is taken off; one of the person's own is removed from the array. The person's own entries are in the order the person made them. A ⭐ entry id is not a card id: it has no place in order, visible, collapsed or hiddenLines. A reader skips an entry whose id is of neither form or that has no items array, reads a repeated id once and a repeated item key once, keeps the first 8 items and ignores an item key it does not know. A writer keeps the entries it skipped.

rememberNever.description: The "remember it?" prompts the person said never to show again, as prompt ids. A prompt offers, in an entry form, to keep a choice just made there as the person's setting: Yes sets it, Later hides the prompt in that form only (stored nowhere), Never adds its id here. Ids are defined by hds-webapp; today 'charting-method' (the offer to make the method of a cervical-fluid observation the person's charting method), 'input-method:' followed by an item key (the offer to keep the method chosen in the entry form of a convertible item other than cervical fluid as that item's preferred-input setting) and 'unit:' followed by an item key (the offer to keep the unit chosen in the entry form of an item with variations as that item's preferred-input setting). The item key is everything after the first ':'. An id names a prompt, never the value offered or declined; the item key in it only says which item's form the prompt was in, so an id can say which items the person enters: personal data as the rest of the event. Absent, empty or not an array: none. A reader ignores an id it does not know, or whose item key it does not know, and reads a repeated id once. A writer keeps the ids it does not know. An id leaves only when the person asks for that prompt again; a writer then removes only ids of the forms named here ('charting-method', and ids starting 'input-method:' or 'unit:') and keeps every other. An id stays once the setting is set elsewhere. Holds no observation and no choice: the setting itself lives where it always does (the charting method and the preferred-input settings in HDSSettings).

settings/hds-webapp-read.description: Where the person stopped reading each conversation in hds-webapp, held as a single recurring event on the webapp-settings app stream and updated in place, so the unread count is the same on every device. Holds no health data and no message content: only contact keys and times. A writer re-reads the event just before writing, keeps per contact the later of the two times, and writes the whole object back; Pryv updates are not conditional, so two devices writing at once can lose one update, which only shows read messages as unread again. A writer may drop the keys of contacts that no longer exist. Additional properties are permitted, as for the other hds-webapp settings types.

v.description: Optional version of this settings shape, set by hds-webapp when it changes the meaning of a key, so a reader can migrate an older event.

lastRead.description: Per contact, the time (Pryv event time of the message, seconds) of the newest message the person has read: a message counts as unread when its time is later. The key is the counterparty's lowercased username@host (hds-lib's contact key), or its access id for a contact with no username. A contact with no entry has no marker: its unread count is unknown, not zero.

delivery/composite-v1.description: Per-baby delivery / birth event. One event per baby; siblings of multifetal pregnancies share event.time (= delivery date) and typically share 'mode'. Stillbirth status is carried upstream on fertility-pregnancy.outcome=stillbirth, NOT here. Field vocabularies aligned to LOINC: 73762-7 (mode), 8339-4 (birth weight), 76689-9 (sex assigned at birth), 9274-2 (5-min APGAR).

mode.description: Final route and method of delivery (LOINC 73762-7 / US Standard Certificate of Live Birth).

sex.description: Sex assigned at birth (LOINC 76689-9). 'indeterminate' covers ambiguous genitalia / disorders of sex development.

nicuLengthOfStayDays.description: Length of NICU admission in days; 0 if not admitted.

neonatalDeathDays.description: Days from delivery to neonatal death (within 28 days post-livebirth). Absent / null = alive at last follow-up.

cervix-position/3d-vectors.description: Cervical position observation as up to four 0–1 vectors: height (low→high), firmness (firm→soft), openness (closed→open) follow the SHOW fertility direction (0 = least fertile, 1 = most fertile). Optional tilt (straight→tilted) is a position-only field, not a fertility signal — RYB-originated; no clinical-coding convention exists.

openness.description: Cervical os openness: 0 = closed, 0.5 = medium, 1 = open

tilt.description: Cervix tilt: 0 = straight, 0.5 = medium, 1 = tilted. Position-only — not a fertility signal. Added in body-vulva-cervix-position v2 (RYB-originated; no clinical-coding convention).

mood/5d-vectors.description: Mood observation as five 0–1 dimensional vectors based on Russell's Circumplex and PAD models. Content is { vectors, source? }. Used with the euclidian-distance converter engine.

valence.description: Pleasure/displeasure: 0 = very unpleasant, 0.5 = neutral, 1 = very pleasant

arousal.description: Energy/activation: 0 = very calm, 0.5 = moderate, 1 = very activated

dominance.description: Sense of control: 0 = powerless, 0.5 = neutral, 1 = in control

source.description: Provenance: which method produced this vector. Absent = direct vector input.

key.description: Source method identifier (e.g. mira, hds, descriptive)

sourceData.description: Raw observation from the source method

message/hds-chat-v1.description: DEPRECATED, read path only: pre-CMC chat message on an app chat stream, content is the plain message string. Superseded by the upstream 'message/chat-cmc' type, which the CMC plugin delivers to the peer and whose content is an object. Nothing writes this type any more; hds-webapp still reads it so existing conversations stay visible (see DiaryItem.ts). Declared here because appStreams.yaml's 'chat' entry references it and the model must resolve every eventType it names.

message/system-alert.description: Operator → user notification on app-system-out. Content: { level, title, body, ackRequired?, ackId? }. Plan 45.

ackRequired.description: If true, the user's app surfaces an Acknowledge button and the operator expects a matching message/system-ack

ackId.description: UUID generated by the operator at post time. Echoed in the matching message/system-ack to link the response.

message/system-ack.description: User → operator acknowledgement of a message/system-alert, paired by ackId. Plan 45.

ackedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp at which the user clicked Acknowledge

userNote.description: Optional free-text note from the user (max 1000 chars)

message/hds-reader-v1.description: SUPERSEDED by message/hds-conversation-v1 (4.22.0, documentation/CONVERSATION.md): no new writer; kept so the demo events written before it still validate. One message of the HDS Reader dialogue on the person's account (stream hds-reader-dialogue):the reading of a document, the engine's questions, the person's answers, access requests and job state. content.kind discriminates; each kind is a closed object. Every event of a document carries clientData.related.<document event id>: true, and every event id in content is mirrored there. The values read are on reading events, so a grant on this stream reads them. See documentation/HDS-READER.md.

oneOf.description: job (engine): the state of the reading of one document. Append-only: the latest job event of a document is its state.

engine.description: Stable id of the reading program, lowercase (hds-reader); the <tool> of the sourceKey it writes.

engineVersion.description: The program's version, semver MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional pre-release.

kbVersion.description: The version of the knowledge-base pack the program used, semver MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.

backend.description: Opaque id of the program's backend configuration record that read the printed line, never parsed (for example <runtime>:<model>, or text-layer when no backend ran). No spaces; never a URL, a host name, a device name or a user name.

counts.description: Counts only, never what was counted.

errorCode.description: With status error: a code, never a message.

oneOf.description: notice (engine): a message the app renders from its code. Never model or free text.

about.description: The candidateId the message is about, or document for the document as a whole (document is reserved, never a candidateId).

oneOf.description: reading (engine): one printed line as read, and what the engine proposes to write. Holds what the document prints on that line.

candidateId.description: Opaque id of this candidate, derived by the engine from the document and the record. A reading is never updated once answered: a re-read writes a new candidateId. Never parsed.

printed.description: What the document prints on this line, exactly.

anchor.description: Where the value was printed in the source document (the file/xds-v1 event in clientData.related): an attachment, a page and a box, nothing of what is printed there. See documentation/PROVENANCE.md.

attachmentId.description: The id of the document event's attachment (Pryv attachments[].id) the value was read from.

page.description: Page number within that attachment, from 1 (an image is page 1).

bbox.description: [x, y, width, height] of the printed line the value was read from, in percent of the page as displayed (x and width of its width, y and height of its height), origin at the top left. Absent when the reader has no box it trusts.

confidence.description: The engine's confidence in the reading, 0..1.

proposal.description: The event the engine proposes to write once confirmed. Absent when nothing is proposed.

content.description: The content as it would be stored, valid against type.

time.description: The event time, Unix seconds. Absent when the document prints no usable date (a which-date question is asked).

clientData.description: The clientData keys of the proposed event that the model defines for a lab result (documentation/BLOOD-CHEMISTRY.md, PARTIAL-DATES.md).

hdsTimePrecision.description: No minute (no zone in v1) and no approx (no hdsTimeText).

status.description: clear: proposed, may be confirmed in a batch; check: proposed, asked one by one; unmapped: read, no event proposed (see reason); unit-missing: the line prints no unit; kept-aside: read; no item can hold it yet; kept for a later offer (see reason, requestKey). Unlike unmapped, the line is a metric the Reader can name (a requestKey), only no item holds it; set at reading time, never after an answer.

reason.description: Why the reading is not written: a closed reason code. A line that is not clinical, about a special category or about another person never becomes a reading (documentation/HDS-READER.md).

requestKey.description: The item-request key derived for this metric (specimen and LOINC code, else specimen, language and normalised label tokens), so a kept-aside reading can be offered again once an item ships. No spaces, no control characters.

kbEntries.description: Ids of the knowledge-base entries the mapping rests on. Empty when none does.

askOneByOne.description: true: never offered in a batch (a check, or a mapping resting on a community-tier entry).

specimenImplied.description: true: the document does not print the specimen and a reviewed knowledge-base entry implies it; the app says so.

oneOf.description: question (engine): a closed question to the person.

about.description: The candidateId the message is about, or document for the document as a whole (document is reserved, never a candidateId).

options.description: The choices offered, as codes the app labels (a specimen, a UCUM code, an item key, yes, no). Absent for which-date (the person enters a date) and is-this-yours (answered with confirm or not-mine).

oneOf.description: answer (the person's app): the person's answer to a reading or a question.

inReplyTo.description: The id of the reading or question event answered, mirrored in clientData.related. Idempotency is per candidateId (documentation/HDS-READER.md rule 5).

action.description: confirm, correct (with value), not-mine (the document is not about the person), skip, choose (with option), request-item (opt in to request an item for this metric), duplicate (the person's app found the value already recorded).

candidateIds.description: The candidates the answer covers: required on every answer to a reading (the answered one included; several for a batch) and on every answer to a question about a candidate (that candidate). Absent on an answer to a document-level question.

option.description: With choose: the option picked, one of the question's options.

value.description: With correct: the value as the person corrects it, on the scale of eventType.

eventType.description: With correct: the eventType (unit) the corrected value is in, when it differs from the proposal.

itemKey.description: With correct: the item the person moves the value to, when it differs from the proposal.

time.description: With an answer to which-date: the date the person gives, Unix seconds, placed as PARTIAL-DATES.md places it for timePrecision.

timePrecision.description: With an answer to which-date: how much of time is known.

oneOf.description: access-request (engine): the engine asks for create-only on streams it must write to; the request itself goes through the CMC scope request.
access-result (the person's app): the outcome of an access-request.

inReplyTo.description: The id of the access-request event, mirrored in clientData.related.

oneOf.description: written (engine): one confirmed value was written. The engine's record of its own writes (it cannot read the stream it wrote to).

eventId.description: The id of the value event written, mirrored in clientData.related.

oneOf.description: summary (engine): the outcome of the reading of one document.

keptAside.description: The readings kept aside, by reference: their text and requestKey are on the reading events only, joined by candidateId.

reason.description: Why the reading is not written: a closed reason code. A line that is not clinical, about a special category or about another person never becomes a reading (documentation/HDS-READER.md).

message/hds-conversation-v1.description: One structured item of a conversation between the person and a contact (a doctor, a reading service such as the HDS Reader, a third party's counterparty), on the person's account in the relationship's child of conversation-items: the contact's questions, proposed values and proposed document date and kind (direction received), the person's answers (direction sent). content.kind discriminates; each kind is a closed object. Every event carries clientData.related.<document event id>: true (about), and every event id in content is mirrored there. Proposed values hold what the document prints, so a grant on the child reads them; nothing of them travels over CMC (alerts carry ids and counts only). Supersedes message/hds-reader-v1. See documentation/CONVERSATION.md.

oneOf.description: question (the contact, on received): a closed question to the person about one document, with what she needs to answer it without the document.

about.description: The event id of the document the question is about (a file/xds-v1 event shared in the relationship), mirrored in clientData.related.

code.description: What is asked, a code the app renders. Bare codes are HDS's and listed in documentation/CONVERSATION.md (which-specimen, which-unit, which-analyte, which-date, is-fasting, is-this-yours, which-document-kind, which-document-date, which-row-date, which-column-date); a third party's own codes start with x-<vendor>-. An unknown code is shown, not answerable.

candidateId.description: The candidate the question is about, the candidateId of a proposed-value (or, for which-document-kind and which-document-date, of a proposed-document) on the same child. Absent for a question about the whole document.

options.description: The choices offered, as codes the app labels (a specimen code, a UCUM code, an item key, a document kind key, yes, no). Absent for which-date, which-document-date, which-row-date and which-column-date (the person enters a date) and is-this-yours (answered with confirm or not-mine).

items.description: One choice, a code (up to 128 characters: an item key).

context.description: What the document prints that the person needs to answer: identity (is-this-yours only), dates (which-date and which-document-date only), anchor (is-this-yours: where the identity is printed; which-row-date: the box asked about; which-column-date: the column's heading), grid (which-row-date only: that box), column (which-column-date only: that column). Identity and dates are copied verbatim from the document's text layer, never produced or completed by a model.

identity.description: is-this-yours only: the patient's name and birth date as the document prints them, copied verbatim from its text layer (never produced or completed by a model), so the person can answer without the document.

birthDay.description: birthDate as a day, only when it is unambiguous (a four-digit year).

dates.description: which-date and which-document-date only: the dates the document prints (never the birth date), so the person can pick one without the document. Partial dates are not listed.

text.description: The date as printed, the date only.

label.description: The label printed before it (e.g. Édité le), never a person's name.

grid.description: A dated grid only: the box. Her app orders, groups and names boxes from it, never from bbox. See documentation/CONVERSATION.md.

row.description: The grid's row on its page, from the top, from 1, every row of the printed grid counted, the empty ones too.

column.description: which-column-date only: the result column of a table read column by column, on the anchor's page. See documentation/CONVERSATION.md.

index.description: The result column, from the left, from 1, every result column the table prints counted, the empty ones too.

anchor.description: Where the value was printed in the source document (the file/xds-v1 event in clientData.related): the document, an attachment, a page and a box, nothing of what is printed there. Self-contained: whoever may read both the event and the document finds the zone from the anchor alone. See documentation/PROVENANCE.md.

eventId.description: The id of the file/xds-v1 document event, the one clientData.related names (it stays there for queries). Absent on anchors written before 4.25.0: the document is then the one related names.

attachmentId.description: The id of the document event's attachment (Pryv attachments[].id) the value was read from.

page.description: Page number within that attachment, from 1 (an image is page 1).

bbox.description: [x, y, width, height] of the printed line the value was read from, in percent of the page as displayed (x and width of its width, y and height of its height), origin at the top left. Absent when the reader has no box it trusts.

oneOf.description: proposed-value (the contact, on received): one line (or one part of a box of a dated grid) as read from a document, and the event the contact proposes; the person's app writes it once she confirms. Holds what the document prints on that line.

about.description: The event id of the document the value was read from, mirrored in clientData.related.

candidateId.description: Opaque id of this candidate, derived by the contact from the document, the record and the proposal: the same on every re-read while the proposal is the same, a new one when it differs. Never parsed.

replaces.description: The candidateId of a proposed value of the same document that this one replaces (a re-proposal after the person answered a question about it); the replaced one is no longer confirmable.

printed.description: What the document prints or bears there, exactly. value is absent only with reason not-read (documentation/CONVERSATION.md).

samplingTime.description: The sampling time printed over the value's column on a report with one column per sampling, normalised to HH:MM (24 h), so two same-day values can be told apart. Display only: never the value's time, never sent over CMC.

anchor.description: Where the value was printed in the source document (the file/xds-v1 event in clientData.related): the document, an attachment, a page and a box, nothing of what is printed there. Self-contained: whoever may read both the event and the document finds the zone from the anchor alone. See documentation/PROVENANCE.md.

eventId.description: The id of the file/xds-v1 document event, the one clientData.related names (it stays there for queries). Absent on anchors written before 4.25.0: the document is then the one related names.

attachmentId.description: The id of the document event's attachment (Pryv attachments[].id) the value was read from.

page.description: Page number within that attachment, from 1 (an image is page 1).

bbox.description: [x, y, width, height] of the printed line the value was read from, in percent of the page as displayed (x and width of its width, y and height of its height), origin at the top left. Absent when the reader has no box it trusts.

grid.description: A dated grid only: the box. Her app orders, groups and names boxes from it, never from bbox. See documentation/CONVERSATION.md.

row.description: The grid's row on its page, from the top, from 1, every row of the printed grid counted, the empty ones too.

column.description: A table read column by column on a picture only (which-column-date): the value's result column, on its anchor's page. Her app groups values under their column's question from it. See documentation/CONVERSATION.md.

index.description: The result column, from the left, from 1, every result column the table prints counted, the empty ones too.

proposal.description: The event the contact proposes; the person's app writes it once she confirms. Absent when nothing is proposed.

content.description: The content as it would be stored, valid against type.

time.description: The event time, Unix seconds. Absent when the document prints no usable date (a which-date question is asked).

clientData.description: The clientData keys of the proposed event that the model defines for a lab result (documentation/BLOOD-CHEMISTRY.md, PARTIAL-DATES.md).

hdsTimePrecision.description: No minute (no zone in v1) and no approx (no hdsTimeText).

status.description: clear: proposed, may be confirmed in a batch; check: proposed, asked one by one; unmapped: read or seen, no event proposed (see reason); unit-missing: the line prints no unit; kept-aside: read; no item can hold it yet; kept for a later offer (see reason, requestKey). Set when the line is read, never after an answer.

reason.description: Why nothing is proposed: a closed reason code. A line that is not clinical, about a special category or about another person never becomes a proposed value (documentation/CONVERSATION.md).

requestKey.description: The item-request key derived for this metric (specimen and LOINC code, else specimen, language and normalised label tokens), so a kept-aside value can be offered again once an item ships. No spaces, no control characters.

askOneByOne.description: true: never offered in a batch (a check, or a mapping resting on a community-tier entry).

specimenImplied.description: true: the document does not print the specimen and a reviewed knowledge-base entry implies it; the app says so.

extraction.description: The program that read the line: the person's app copies these four fields into clientData.hdsExtraction of the value it writes, after checking engine against the relationship (documentation/CONVERSATION.md).

engine.description: Stable id of the reading program, lowercase (hds-reader); the <tool> of the sourceKey it writes.

engineVersion.description: The program's version, semver MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional pre-release.

kbVersion.description: The version of the knowledge-base pack the program used, semver MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.

backend.description: Opaque id of the program's backend configuration record that read the printed line, never parsed (for example <runtime>:<model>, or text-layer when no backend ran). No spaces; never a URL, a host name, a device name or a user name.

oneOf.description: proposed-document (the contact, on received): the date and the kind the contact proposes for a document the person added without them (clientData.hdsDocumentPending on the document event, documentation/DOCUMENTS.md). Her app applies a field once she confirms, and only while that field is still pending. Carries a pack kind key and a date, nothing printed.

about.description: The event id of the document (a file/xds-v1 event shared in the relationship) the date and kind are proposed for, mirrored in clientData.related.

candidateId.description: Opaque id of this proposal, derived by the contact from the document, its attachment and the proposal: the same on every re-read while the proposal is the same, a new one when it differs. Never parsed.

replaces.description: The candidateId of a proposed-document of the same document that this one replaces (the contact learned more, e.g. her answer to which-date); the replaced one is no longer confirmable.

anchor.description: Where the proposed date is printed in the document: the document, an attachment, a page and a box, nothing of what is printed there (documentation/PROVENANCE.md).

page.description: Page number within that attachment, from 1 (an image is page 1).

extraction.description: The program that read the document, when one did. Optional: a person (a doctor) may propose a date and a kind; no vouching applies, since only a pack key and a date reach the document, on her tap.

engineVersion.description: The program's version, semver MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH with an optional pre-release.

kbVersion.description: The version of the knowledge-base pack the program used, semver MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.

backend.description: Opaque id of the program's backend configuration record that read the printed line, never parsed (for example <runtime>:<model>, or text-layer when no backend ran). No spaces; never a URL, a host name, a device name or a user name.

oneOf.description: answer (the person's app, on sent): the person's answer to a proposed value, a proposed document or a question. Only confirm and correct on a proposed value write a value: her app writes it first and lists it in written. Confirm and correct on a proposed document update the document: her app lists the fields it wrote in applied, never in written. An answer to a question (choose included) writes nothing. note carries her own comment, removed by her app after the work on the document is done.

inReplyTo.description: The id of the proposed-value, proposed-document or question event answered, mirrored in clientData.related.

about.description: The event id of the document the answered event is about, mirrored in clientData.related.

action.description: confirm, correct (her app wrote a value she changed; the value does not travel), not-mine (the document is not about the person), skip, choose (with option), request-item (opt in to request an item for this metric), duplicate (the person's app found the value already recorded).

candidateIds.description: The candidates the answer covers: required on every answer to a proposed value (the answered one included; several for a batch) and on every answer to a question about a candidate (that candidate). Absent on an answer to a document-level question.

option.description: With choose: the option picked, one of the question's options.

time.description: With an answer to which-date or which-document-date: the date the person gives, Unix seconds, placed as PARTIAL-DATES.md places it for timePrecision.

timePrecision.description: With an answer to which-date or which-document-date: how much of time is known.

basis.description: An answer the person's app gave without a tap, and why. profile-match: a confirm on is-this-yours, the printed identity matches her profile. existing-value: a duplicate on proposed values, each already in her record (same item, same day, equal value; documentation/CONVERSATION.md, A value she already has). not-pending: a skip on a proposed document none of whose proposed fields is pending on the document any more (4.26.0). Absent when she answered herself.

written.description: The value events her app wrote for this answer, one per candidate, mirrored in clientData.related: the contact's record that a candidate is written (it cannot read the event), and her app's list of what to delete after a later not-mine. Never on an answer to a proposed document (applied).

eventId.description: The id of the value event written.

applied.description: With confirm or correct on a proposed document: the document's fields her app wrote (time, kind), only those still pending (4.26.0). Never with written.

note.description: Her own comment on what she answers, plain text, on any action (a comment alone is a skip with a note). Never changes the action's meaning, never in an alert, never echoed by the contact; her app removes it once the work on the document is done (documentation/CONVERSATION.md, R10).

questionnaire/request-v1.description: A questionnaire instantiated for this patient, as asked by a doctor or a generator. It is written into the patient's account ('requester', set by the patient's own app, records who asked); no event travels between two accounts. Carries a 'questions' map keyed by stable question keys. Each question references an existing HDS item (itemRef) with optional entity filter (params), a temporal scope (ever / window / latest with withinDays), and an optional subField for qualifier capture. The patient's matching questionnaire/answer-v1 event carries the answers map keyed by the same question keys and links back via requestEventId. Question keys must match Pryv content-query path grammar [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+ so content.answers.<key>.status queries work. See documentation/QUESTIONNAIRE.md.

title.description: Optional localized title shown to the patient

description.description: Optional localized description / instructions shown above the questionnaire

templateRef.description: Optional reference to a saved hds-lib appTemplates Questionnaire definition that this request was generated from

requester.description: Who asked, from the person's side. Written by the person's app when it materializes a questionnaire bundled in an accepted request, from the accept result, never copied from the offer. Absent on requests written before data-model 3.49.0. When the event's createdBy is a relationship's own access, that relationship is the requester and this field is not needed. See documentation/QUESTIONNAIRE.md § Who asked.

relationship.description: The CMC relationship: the base id (pryv.utils.parseAccessRef(id).base, without its serial) of the access the person granted the requester at accept, as hds-lib cmcDocuments.relationshipIdOf returns it and as document shares store it (hdsDocumentShare.relationship). An id in the person's own account, meaningful there only.

questions.description: Map of questionKey → question definition. Keys must respect the Pryv content-query path grammar [a-zA-Z0-9_-]+ — no colons, dots, or array indices.

label.description: Localized question text shown to the patient

itemRef.description: Key of an existing HDS item (data-model items registry) that defines storage shape + renderer for the answer's referenced events

params.description: Optional filter narrowing the question to a specific entity (e.g. { drug: { codes: [...] } } for a medication question). Shape is interpreted by the referenced item's renderer.

scope.description: Temporal scope evaluated by the renderer for prefill / matching event lookup

subField.description: Optional qualifier capture rendered alongside the answer when status is 'answered'. Stored as 'qualifier' on the answer entry.

questionnaire/answer-v1.description: The patient's response to a questionnaire/request-v1, written by the patient's app into the patient's own account. Nothing sends it to the requester: the requester reads it only under a grant on the stream it is in. 'requestEventId' links back to the request event. 'answers' is a map keyed by the same question keys as the request; key absence means 'not-answered' (skipped / unreached). Each answer entry carries a 'status' enum (answered / no / unknown / declined) with conditional fields per status. Referenced event ids in 'answered' entries must ALSO be mirrored into clientData.related.<eventId>: true per the Pryv §7 keyed-object cross-reference convention so cohort queries can use the indexed clientData parameter. See documentation/QUESTIONNAIRE.md.

requestEventId.description: eventId of the questionnaire/request-v1 event being answered

answers.description: Map of questionKey → answer entry. Keys present here MUST correspond to questions in the linked request. Key absence = implicit 'not-answered' (skipped or unreached).

references.description: eventIds of the typed events that satisfy this question. Non-empty. Each id MUST also appear as a key in clientData.related (with value true) on the same event.

qualifier.description: Optional sub-field value (trimester, free text, number, etc.). Shape interpreted by the request's subField declaration.

reason.description: Optional free-text reason for declining to answer (v1). Future additive extension may accept a coded value (e.g. SNOMED 715169006 'Declined to disclose information').

sync-status/bridge.description: Sync watermark written by a data source (a bridge, or an app syncing into the user's own account) recording how far it has synced, so its next run can read it back. Content is deliberately open: writers already carry different payloads (`syncedUntil`, `action`, `changeLogs`, a plugin/bridge version). `syncedUntil` is the one agreed field — set it when the source has a meaningful high-water mark, so a viewer can generically show 'last synced from <app>'. Written to a bridge's per-user stream (a bridge's resume watermark stays on the bridge's own account), or to the app-stream `sync` suffix when the writer is an app on the user's own account. A connector's user-visible status is not this type: it goes to the user's `sync-status` stream tree as `sync-status/connector-v1`.

syncedUntil.description: High-water mark the source has synced up to. Unix time in seconds, or an ISO-8601 timestamp.

error.description: Error recorded by the source for this sync run, when one occurred.

sync-status/connector-v1.description: Status of one connected service. One event per connector stream, updated in place; times are Unix seconds.

consent/record-v1.description: One account-level consent act on one version of one legal document.

research/eligibility-band-v1.description: The result a person chose to send for the eligibility test of a study: the request and the band of her score (below 50, or 50 and more), nothing else. The test runs on her device. One event per request, updated when she sends again. See documentation/ELIGIBILITY.md.

band.description: Band of the unrounded score, in %.

research/topics-v1.description: The research topics a person chose, to receive the research invitations that concern them: one event, updated in place. An empty list means none chosen. Keys of the research-topic vocabulary only, no free text. See documentation/RESEARCH.md.

support/conversation-v1.description: State of one support conversation, kept on the support group's account: one event per conversation, updated in place by the support service and the team's members; times are Unix seconds. Holds no health data, no message text and no email address. See documentation/SUPPORT.md.

userSlug.description: The person's counterparty slug (<username>--<host-slug>, as @pryv/cmc counterpartySlug builds it): the last segment of the conversation's thread stream on the group account. Identifies the conversation.

status.description: new: the person wrote and no one on the team has it (the thread's first message, or a message after a close); open: the team is handling it; closed: closed by the team.

claimedBy.description: The team member who took the conversation (advisory, not an access control). Absent when no one has it.

membershipAccessId.description: The id of the member's membership access on the group account.

host.description: The host of the member's own account.

displayName.description: The member's display name, in the form the person's byline takes it (at most 40 characters, no colon, no newline); readers fall back to username.

notify.description: The person asked to be told by email when the team answers; written by the support service only. Waiting while sentAt is absent. The address itself is never here: only the support service holds it.

consentAt.description: When the person consented to the email.

file/xds-v1.description: A medical document (lab report, letter, prescription, imaging or procedure report, administrative document) as one or more Pryv attachments, with the IHE XDS / CH:EPR DocumentEntry metadata as validated content, so HDS can publish it as a FHIR DocumentReference or an XDS DocumentEntry without reading clientData. Codings follow FHIR Coding: system is a URI (http://snomed.info/sct, http://loinc.org). class and type take their codes from the CH:EPR value sets http://fhir.ch/ig/ch-term/ValueSet/DocumentEntry.classCode and .typeCode. The attachment's own integrity is its sha256; the XDS SHA-1 hash and the confidentiality code are not stored, because they are set at publication. See documentation/DOCUMENTS.md.

class.description: The document's class: DocumentEntry.classCode, FHIR DocumentReference.category. One coding.

version.description: The code system version, when it matters (an edition of SNOMED CT, such as the Swiss extension).

type.description: The document's type: DocumentEntry.typeCode first, then other codings of the same type (a CDA document code, the source system's code). FHIR DocumentReference.type.

version.description: The code system version, when it matters (an edition of SNOMED CT, such as the Swiss extension).

title.description: The document's title as printed, or as the person named it. Shown to every reader of the stream.

language.description: The document's language, a BCP-47 tag (fr, de-CH); und when it is not known.

creation.description: When the document was written, ISO 8601 as FHIR dateTime: a year, a year-month, a date, or a date-time with its offset (2026, 2026-10, 2026-10-28, 2026-10-28T09:30:00+01:00), when it differs from the event time. The event time is when the document belongs on the person's timeline.

status.description: current, or superseded once a newer document replaces this one. A replacement is a new event that lists this one in 'supersedes'; this event stays. A reader treats a document as superseded when another document supersedes it, whatever this field says.

supersedes.description: Event ids of the documents this one replaces (DocumentEntry relationship RPLC). Each id is mirrored in clientData.related.<eventId> (documentation/PROVENANCE.md).

authors.description: Who wrote the document: DocumentEntry.author, FHIR DocumentReference.author. eventId points at a provider event (provider/practitioner-v1 or provider/organization-v1) when one exists (mirrored in clientData.related); name, organization and service are free text as printed, kept beside eventId, and are shown to every reader of the stream.

eventId.description: Event id of the author's provider event: provider/practitioner-v1 (a person) or provider/organization-v1 (a practice, clinic, hospital or laboratory). Mirrored in clientData.related.<eventId> (documentation/PROVENANCE.md).

version.description: The code system version, when it matters (an edition of SNOMED CT, such as the Swiss extension).

encounterId.description: Event id of the encounter (an encounter/visit-v1 event) the document comes from, when one is recorded (mirrored in clientData.related).

version.description: The code system version, when it matters (an edition of SNOMED CT, such as the Swiss extension).
The code system version, when it matters (an edition of SNOMED CT, such as the Swiss extension).
The code system version, when it matters (an edition of SNOMED CT, such as the Swiss extension).

event.description: DocumentEntry.eventCodeList: the main acts or conditions the document is about, FHIR DocumentReference.event.

version.description: The code system version, when it matters (an edition of SNOMED CT, such as the Swiss extension).

pages.description: Number of pages of the original, when known.

uniqueId.description: The document's own global identifier, set by the system that issued it (an EPR, a laboratory system), never made up by a writer: DocumentEntry.uniqueId, FHIR DocumentReference.masterIdentifier, as a FHIR Identifier {system, value}. One per version: a replacement document has its own. An OID or a UUID is always stored as system urn:ietf:rfc:3986 with value urn:oid:<oid> or urn:uuid:<uuid in lower case> (IHE ITI TF-2 Appendix Z.9.1), however the source spells it. Mirrored in clientData.hdsDocumentUniqueId as <system>|<value>, the key that recognises a document already held (documentation/DOCUMENTS.md).

system.description: A URI. Not urn:oid:<root> (in any case): that is the root-plus-extension form, which has no settled mapping and is not stored (documentation/DOCUMENTS.md, Open points). urn:ietf:rfc:3986 is written in lower case only.

temperature/disturbance-v1.description: Reason a basal body temperature reading is unreliable ('parasitic temperature'). Qualifier for a co-occurring body-temperature-basal event: sympto-thermal rules EXCLUDE disturbed readings from the coverline and temperature-shift computation, so a consumer charting BBT must be able to see the flag. Absence of this event means the reading was not flagged, not that it was confirmed reliable.

lifestyle/use-status-v1.description: Lifetime use status for a substance or habit: never used, used in the past, uses now. A coded status, not a severity or a quantity.

lifestyle/diet-pattern-v1.description: Overall dietary pattern, as a single mutually exclusive choice.

lifestyle/diet-restriction-v1.description: Foods avoided, by choice, belief or medical need. Array: several restrictions hold at once. Each event is a complete dated snapshot of the restrictions in force — one that ends simply does not appear in the next snapshot. An empty array means no restriction.

lifestyle/frequency-band-v1.description: Coded frequency band for a habitual behaviour. Bands are ranges, so no scalar encoding exists that does not invent a value the respondent never gave, and unlike ratio/proportion a frequency has no "maximum" anchor to normalise against. An item selects the subset of bands its instrument defines; any per-instrument score is positional over the item options and is derived on the reader side.

lab-result/coded-v1.description: A laboratory result for an analyte with no item of its own, coded in content and stored as printed. 'analyte' is the coded test (LOINC whenever a verified code exists); the result is a number in its UCUM unit, possibly a limit ('comparator'), and/or the result as printed ('valueText'). Never converted. Maps to FHIR Observation: analyte → code, value/comparator/unit → valueQuantity, valueCodes/valueText → valueCodeableConcept/valueString. See documentation/BLOOD-CHEMISTRY.md.

analyte.description: The coded test. Coded by the writer from a curated table: 'hdsId' is absent until a datasource provides one, and a datasource that does emits canonical URI systems.

label.description: The test name, by language; 'en' is required.

codes.description: FHIR Codings of the test: one LOINC entry (system http://loinc.org) whenever a verified code exists, otherwise the lab's own code system.

system.description: Canonical URI of the code system (http://loinc.org, urn:oid:…).

version.description: The code system version, when it matters.

display.description: The code system's display name (LOINC Long Common Name).

hdsId.description: The datasource id of the test, when a datasource provides one.

value.description: The figure as printed; with 'comparator', the printed limit.

comparator.description: The value is a limit, not an exact figure: the true value is below, at most, above, at least it (FHIR Quantity.comparator).

unit.description: UCUM code of the printed unit, case-sensitive ('umol/L', '{copies}/mL', '1' when unitless). Printable ASCII, no space.

unitText.description: The unit exactly as printed ('µmol/l', 'mUI/mL'), for display.

valueText.description: The result exactly as printed when it is not only a number ('negative', 'détecté', '1:160', '< LOQ').

valueCodes.description: The printed qualitative result as FHIR Codings (CodeableConcept.coding), with 'valueText': a SNOMED CT qualifier value, and the lab's own result code when it printed one.

notes.description: The comment printed with the result ('haemolysed sample').

genetic-variant/coded-v1.description: The result of a genetic test for one variant of one gene, as the laboratory reported it: one event per tested variant, event.time the sample collection date. 'gene' and 'variant' are coded (HGNC; HGVS, dbSNP, ClinVar) with the labels as printed; 'result' is whether the variant was found, 'zygosity' its allelic state when printed. Lives under the 'genetics' root, which only an explicit grant covers. Maps to the HL7 Genomics Reporting variant Observation: gene → 48018-6, variant → 81252-9 / 48004-6, result → 69548-6, zygosity → 53034-5. The laboratory eventId is mirrored in clientData.related.<eventId> (documentation/PROVENANCE.md). See documentation/GENETICS.md.

gene.description: The gene studied (LOINC 48018-6): the symbol as printed, and its HGNC code (system http://www.genenames.org/geneId, code 'HGNC:7436', display the approved symbol).

codes.description: FHIR Codings of the gene: the HGNC entry.

variant.description: The variant tested (LOINC 81252-9, DNA change 48004-6): the lab's label as printed, and its codes when known: HGVS (system http://varnomen.hgvs.org, the c. string with its transcript, 'NM_005957.5:c.665C>T'), dbSNP (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/projects/SNP, 'rs1801133'), ClinVar (http://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/clinvar).

label.description: The variant as the lab printed it ('C677T').

codes.description: FHIR Codings of the variant: HGVS, dbSNP and/or ClinVar.

result.description: Whether the variant was found, LOINC 69548-6 answer list LL1971-2: present LA9633-4, absent LA9634-2, indeterminate LA11884-6, no-call LA18198-4. A variant reported as detected with no zygosity printed is 'present' alone.

zygosity.description: The allelic state as printed, LOINC 53034-5 answer list LL381-5: homozygous LA6705-3, heterozygous LA6706-1, hemizygous LA6707-9, homoplasmic LA6704-6, heteroplasmic LA6703-8. Meaningful with 'present' only (advisory, not enforced).

resultText.description: The result exactly as printed ('C677T homozygote', 'non détecté').

method.description: The test method or panel as printed ('PCR', 'Thrombophilia panel').

laboratory.description: The laboratory that performed the test: eventId points at a provider/organization-v1 event when one exists, name is the name as printed, kept beside it; at least one of the two. The eventId is mirrored in clientData.related.<eventId> (documentation/PROVENANCE.md).

eventId.description: Event id of the laboratory's provider/organization-v1 event.

name.description: The name as printed. Shown to every reader of the stream.

notes.description: The comment printed with the result (an interpretation, a limitation of the test).

encounter/visit-v1.description: A care visit or stay: a consultation, hospital stay, emergency, day case, teleconsultation or home visit. event.time is when it began, event.duration how long it lasted: no duration when the end is not known, null only while a stay is ongoing. Maps to FHIR Encounter: kind → class, specialty → serviceType, reason → reasonCode.text, participants → participant, serviceProvider → serviceProvider, the event period → period; status is derived from the duration, never stored. Every eventId in content is mirrored in clientData.related.<eventId> (documentation/PROVENANCE.md). See documentation/ENCOUNTER.md.

kind.description: The kind of visit, FHIR Encounter.class (the table is in documentation/ENCOUNTER.md).

specialty.description: The clinical specialty of the visit, from DocumentEntry.practiceSettingCode (SNOMED CT, the vocabulary of file/xds-v1 practiceSetting). FHIR Encounter.serviceType.

version.description: The code system version, when it matters (an edition of SNOMED CT, such as the Swiss extension).

reason.description: Why the person was seen, as said or printed. FHIR Encounter.reasonCode.text. Shown to every reader of the stream.

notes.description: Free notes about the visit. Not exported (FHIR R4 Encounter has no note). Shown to every reader of the stream.

participants.description: The practitioners involved, FHIR Encounter.participant: eventId points at a provider/practitioner-v1 event when one exists, name is the name as printed, kept beside it; at least one of the two. role is the FHIR participant type (v3-ParticipationType ATND, REF, CON, ADM, DIS). Each eventId is mirrored in clientData.related.<eventId> (documentation/PROVENANCE.md).

eventId.description: Event id of the practitioner's provider/practitioner-v1 event.

name.description: The name as printed. Shown to every reader of the stream.

role.description: What the practitioner did in this visit: attender (ATND), referrer (REF), consultant (CON), admitter (ADM), discharger (DIS).

serviceProvider.description: The organization the visit took place at, FHIR Encounter.serviceProvider: eventId points at a provider/organization-v1 event when one exists, name is the name as printed, kept beside it; at least one of the two. The eventId is mirrored in clientData.related.<eventId> (documentation/PROVENANCE.md).

eventId.description: Event id of the organization's provider/organization-v1 event.

name.description: The name as printed. Shown to every reader of the stream.

provider/practitioner-v1.description: A care practitioner: a doctor, therapist, midwife or other person who provides care. One event per practitioner, pointed at by visits (encounter/visit-v1 participants[].eventId) and documents (file/xds-v1 authors[].eventId). Maps to FHIR Practitioner, with a PractitionerRole for its specialty and organizations. Every eventId in content is mirrored in clientData.related.<eventId>, the GLN and ZSR in clientData.hdsGln and hdsZsr (documentation/PROVENANCE.md). See documentation/ENCOUNTER.md.

name.description: The name as printed ('Dr méd. Anne Muller'). FHIR HumanName.text. Shown to every reader of the stream.

given.description: Given name(s) as printed, one string ('Anne Marie'). FHIR HumanName.given: the export splits it on spaces.

family.description: Family name as printed. FHIR HumanName.family; CH Core Practitioner requires it (ch-pract-1), so a practitioner without it exports with no CH Core claim.

specialties.description: The practitioner's specialties, FHIR PractitionerRole.specialty (0..*): every specialist title as printed, in printed order. Preferably from MedReg HCProfessional.hcSpecialisation (urn:oid:2.16.756.5.30.1.127.3.5, the value set CH Core PractitionerRole binds); a DocumentEntry.practiceSettingCode (SNOMED CT) is accepted.

version.description: The code system version, when it matters (an edition of SNOMED CT, such as the Swiss extension).

identifiers.description: Official identifiers, FHIR Identifier {system, value}; system is a URI. CH Core Practitioner: GLN urn:oid:2.51.1.3 (at most one), ZSR urn:oid:2.16.756.5.30.1.123.100.2.1.1. Values are stored as printed and not checked here. See documentation/ENCOUNTER.md.

organizations.description: The organizations the practitioner works for, FHIR PractitionerRole.organization: eventId points at a provider/organization-v1 event when one exists, name is the name as printed, kept beside it; at least one of the two. Each eventId is mirrored in clientData.related.<eventId> (documentation/PROVENANCE.md).

eventId.description: Event id of the organization's provider/organization-v1 event.

name.description: The name as printed. Shown to every reader of the stream.

provider/organization-v1.description: A care organization: a practice, clinic, hospital, laboratory, or one of its departments (a department is its own organization). One event per organization, pointed at by visits (encounter/visit-v1 serviceProvider.eventId), practitioners (provider/practitioner-v1 organizations[].eventId) and documents (file/xds-v1 authors[].eventId). Maps to FHIR Organization. The GLN and ZSR are mirrored in clientData.hdsGln and hdsZsr (documentation/PROVENANCE.md). See documentation/ENCOUNTER.md.

name.description: The name as printed ('HUG, Service de cardiologie'). FHIR Organization.name. Shown to every reader of the stream.

identifiers.description: Official identifiers, FHIR Identifier {system, value}; system is a URI. CH Core Organization, at most one each: GLN urn:oid:2.51.1.3, ZSR urn:oid:2.16.756.5.30.1.123.100.2.1.1, UIDB urn:oid:2.16.756.5.35, BER urn:oid:2.16.756.5.45. Values are stored as printed and not checked here. See documentation/ENCOUNTER.md.

correction/entry-v1.description: A professional's correction of one entry of the person's record: a contact holding a CMC relationship (an instructor, a clinician) says that an entry should have been different (change), should exist (add) or should not exist (remove), with an optional comment. The entry itself is never changed by the contact: she applies a correction with her own app if she wants. Written by the contact on its own corr- child of entry-corrections, never updated (superseded by a new one naming it in replaces, withdrawn by trashing it). event.time is the corrected entry's time (for add, the moment the missing entry is about), so a timeline places it next to the entry; readers join it to the entry by entryId, never by time. Every event id in content is mirrored in clientData.related.<eventId> (documentation/PROVENANCE.md). Conditions the schema cannot express (which fields go with which kind, the item checks) are in documentation/CORRECTIONS.md.

kind.description: change: the entry entryId should have been corrected. add: there is no entry, one should exist (corrected). remove: the entry entryId should not exist.

authorRole.description: The author's role, declared by the writer: a role, never an identity. Labels and SNOMED CT occupations in the vocabulary professional-role (definitions/vocabularies/professional.yaml). A reader reads a role it does not know as other.

itemKey.description: The item of the published pack the entry is, or should be, on (not an app's overload item): not a system or attachments item, not under an explicitGrantOnly root.

entryId.description: With change and remove: the id of the corrected event. Mirrored in clientData.related.<entryId>.

entryModified.description: With change and remove: the entry's modified (Unix seconds) as the writer saw it, so a reader tells that the entry changed since.

corrected.description: What the entry should have been, the shape of a conversation proposal (documentation/CONVERSATION.md): type and content together (content valid against type, type an eventType of itemKey), time when the entry belongs on another moment (change only). At least one of type and time; with add, type and content.

content.description: The content as it would be stored, valid against type.

time.description: The time the entry should have, Unix seconds (a day: 12:00 UTC with clientData.hdsTimePrecision day, PARTIAL-DATES.md).

clientData.description: The clientData keys of the corrected entry that the model defines and a correction may set (PARTIAL-DATES.md, MENSTRUAL-CYCLE.md, BLOOD-CHEMISTRY.md).

comment.description: The author's explanation, shown to every reader of the correction. Markdown when the event's clientData.hdsTextFormat is text/markdown (PROVENANCE.md), else plain text.

about.description: The file/xds-v1 document the correction was read from (a chart photo). Mirrored in clientData.related.<about>; with it, clientData.hdsSourceAnchor may point at the box, its eventId = about.

replaces.description: The id of an earlier correction that this one replaces: on the same corr- child, with the same entryId (for add, the same itemKey). Mirrored in clientData.related.<replaces>.
